Rationale: the maintainer's ruling on #9968 (impersonate-user residue + set-role veto tension, same vendor-admin family, same package) will set the posture for consumerless vendor `/admin/` surface; this card's outcome follows it. Expected post-ruling grade: adopt the dev report's recommendation — B with A as the standing state (on-demand re-implementation; record the intended refusal in `auth-route-ledger.ts` so "advertised, refuses the only entitled caller" stops being an undocumented declared≠enforced claim) — unless the #9968 ruling says otherwise. One decision card per family keeps the inbox lean.

Blocked-by: #9968

## Blocker discharged — and it was discharged **2026-08-20**, not today. `pm:blocked` → `needs-user-decision`.

#9968 closed at 03:20Z today (PR #11530 merged, both halves delivered). But reading this card's own blocker rather than inferring from that merge changes the date materially.

### What this card was actually waiting on

The triage note is explicit, and it is the **ruling**, not the delivery:

> blocked behind the family decision rather than escalated as a second inbox card. Rationale: **the maintainer's *ruling* on #9968 … will set the posture for consumerless vendor `/admin/` surface; this card's outcome follows it.**
>
> `Blocked-by: #9968`

That ruling landed **2026-08-20** ("Ruled: B") and was **reaffirmed 2026-08-22**. So the condition this card waits on has been satisfied for four days, and it has been sitting `pm:blocked` behind an already-met condition ever since — independent of today's merge.

Recording that plainly because it is the same board-hygiene class as a card left `pm:queue` after its work landed: a `Blocked-by:` line is only as good as the re-check, and nothing re-checks it automatically. Today's merge makes the discharge unambiguous, but it was not the thing that discharged it.

### ⛔ What I am NOT doing

Moving this to `needs-user-decision` — **routing**, not grading. I am not choosing between the card's own **A** (leave them, record the intended refusal), **B** (re-implement on demand), or **C** (re-implement all seven now). The triage note pre-recorded an expectation ("adopt the dev report's recommendation — B with A as the standing state … **unless the #9968 ruling says otherwise**"), and I am deliberately not converting that expectation into a decision on the maintainer's behalf.

⚠️ One honest qualifier for whoever rules, because the pre-recorded expectation rests on it: the #9968 ruling set a **posture** for the family (retire what is dead; re-implement only what has a real consumer, in the ruled plugin-endpoint shape) — it did **not** address these seven consumerless routes directly. So "unless the #9968 ruling says otherwise" resolves to *it did not say otherwise*, which supports B/A but is weaker than a ruling on this card's own question.

### What is settled and does not need re-deriving

- All seven routes fail **closed** — a platform admin gets `403 YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_*`, identically to a plain member. This is a broken capability claim, **never an escalation**.
- They have **no ObjectStack consumer at all** — no `type: 'api'` action, no console call, no SDK row, no doc pointing at them. They are surface the `rawApp.all(...)` catch-all publishes because better-auth registers it.
- But they **are** published and ledgered in `BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE`, so "advertised but always refuses the only caller entitled to it" is a declared-≠-enforced claim in its own right (Prime Directive #10).
- ⚠️ Two mechanics measured in #9652 that constrain any re-implementation: shadowing a vendor path with a raw Hono mount **silently detaches every better-auth hook keyed on that path** (`/admin/remove-user` carries the break-glass last-local-credential guard — reuse `last-local-credential.ts`, do not reimplement); and `/admin/create-user`'s header-less server-call trust shape is **unique to it** and does not generalise to any of these seven, which all declare `use: [adminMiddleware]`.
- `remove-user` is the one worth watching — closest to a real capability, and it carries that break-glass guard precisely because it is *not* shadowed.

`pm:blocking` retained: #9652 still sits above this family.

Refs: #9968 (closed, both halves delivered) · #9652 (parent; being read separately, not inferred from this) · PR #11530 · PR #10352

分诊席四维分析(维护者 2026-08-24 点名要求;裁决仍归维护者)。

os-decision-facets

一句话问题:七条 better-auth `/admin/` 路由(remove-user、revoke-sessions、list-users 等)对平台管理员一律 403,且全仓零消费者——留着并记录(A)、按需逐条重实现(B)、还是现在补齐七条(C)?

① **实际业务需求**:实测零 ObjectStack 消费者(无 action、无 console 调用、无 SDK 行、无文档指引)。没有任何拉动。→ A/B。
② **项目长远合理性**:「广告着却拒绝唯一有权的调用者」确是 declared≠enforced,但它已被台账(`BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE`)与 dogfood 的 `better-auth-gate` 桶**钉成已知边界**——不是静默漂移;#9652 已确立按需重挂载的成熟模式(ban/unban 已走过)。→ B。
③ **防 AI 犯错**:403 是 fail-closed,无法被利用;风险只是读 OpenAPI 的集成者预期落空——A 的记录即缓解。反而 C 会新增**七条无人调用、无人演练的安全路由**(且其中 shadowing 会静默摘掉 vendor hook,`remove-user` 上挂着 break-glass 守卫)——未使用的安全面是最容易烂的面。→ B,反对 C。
④ **创业阶段不扩散需求**:C 是七条没人要的路由。→ B。

**推荐:B(第一个出现 ObjectStack 消费者的路由按 #9652 模式当场重挂载),A 为常态记录(四轴同向;即卡面自荐)。** `remove-user` 单独盯——它离真实能力最近且带 break-glass 守卫。裁后本卡关闭(裁决即记录,`pm:blocking` 的下游按解锁扫描处理)。**本分析看不见什么**:您对企业客户管理面的产品规划——若 Setup 用户管理近期要吃这几条能力,直接点名哪几条,按 B 提前触发。

## Maintainer ruling recorded — **B, with A as the standing state**; closing

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-24, live PM chat, verbatim: 「接受你的建议。」 on the aligned four-facet analysis above (which adopted this card's own recommendation).

**Ruled:** the seven better-auth `/admin/` routes stay as they are — published, ledgered, refusing platform admins fail-closed, with the refusal pinned by the dogfood `better-auth-gate` bucket. **The moment any of them gains an ObjectStack consumer, that route gets an ObjectStack mount at that moment, using the #9652 pattern** (reuse `last-local-credential.ts` for the break-glass guard; remember shadowing detaches vendor hooks on that path; the create-user header-less trust shape does not generalise). C (build all seven now) is rejected — unexercised security surface. `remove-user` is the named watch item.

Closing **not planned** — the ruling is the record; the B trigger is written above and needs no open card to fire (the first consumer's own card carries the mount work). Downstream `Blocked-by: #9969` lines unlock via the standard scan; seats re-verify on current refs.
